gaps.rationale: Owner/COUNSEL action per docs/legal/2026-10-10-adopted-decisions.md.

declaredStatic.reason: Reversible catalog states defined by the database schema, rather than operational sample data.
declaredStatic.approvedBy: User-approved P3 scope and delegated implementation choices

declaredStatic.reason: D4 final decision text: cells with fewer than 5 people are suppressed; 5 is the adopted safest default (business choice).

feedback.observation: In audit mode the architect must record a verdict per capability (real / decorative / missing / silently-failing) but the capability status enum only expresses build progress, so the verdict has to be smuggled into the rationale prose. The manifest cannot then be queried for 'show me every decorative screen'.
feedback.proposedChange: Add an optional capability field such as auditVerdict with an enum of live, partial, decorative, missing, silently-failing, and teach `report` and `coverage` to summarise by it.

feedback.observation: The single most damaging pattern found in this codebase was a catch block whose body is identical to the try block, so every failure reports success. It defeats RLS observability, hides unapplied migrations and makes a decorative screen indistinguishable from a working one. It is not named in capability-catalog.md or verification.md.
feedback.proposedChange: Add 'catch-and-succeed' to the anti-pattern list in capability-catalog.md, and add a grep-based check to verification.md: a catch block that calls the same success setter as its try block is a defect.

feedback.observation: Several screens substitute demo data when a query returns ZERO ROWS rather than when it errors. This is more dangerous than an error fallback because it fires in normal operation on a quiet month - a VAT screen showed invented tax totals this way. The discovery reference warns about placeholder data but not about this specific trigger.
feedback.proposedChange: In discovery.md and verification.md, state explicitly that a zero-row result must render an empty state and never substitute sample data, and call out financial and compliance screens as absolute.

feedback.observation: Supabase Edge Functions default to verify_jwt=true, which developers read as 'authenticated', but the check is satisfied by the project's public publishable/anon key that ships in every browser bundle. Two service-role functions here relied on it and had no role check of their own. stack-adapters.md does not warn about this.
feedback.proposedChange: Add to the Supabase section of stack-adapters.md: verify_jwt is not authorization; every service-role Edge Function must independently call auth.getUser on the bearer token and check the role, and Access-Control-Allow-Origin should not be '*' on a privileged function.

feedback.observation: The most consequential question in this audit - which migrations are applied to the live project - was unanswerable because the Supabase MCP server was unauthenticated in a non-interactive session. Roughly a third of the security findings had to be stated conditionally.
feedback.proposedChange: Have the audit agent check for live-database reachability at the START of the pass and, when it is missing, say so in the first paragraph of the report and list precisely which findings are conditional on it, rather than discovering the limitation midway.

feedback.observation: A newer local Claude reference added a migration with the initial P3 timestamp. Read-only reconciliation caught the collision before deployment.
feedback.suggestedChange: Inspect all visible branch migration versions before numbering an additive migration and exercise the full target chain in isolated Postgres.

feedback.observation: placeholder-scan rejects any tests[] entry whose path contains 'mock', so the release-path guard web_platform/tests/no-mock-data.test.mjs cannot be cited as a screen or capability test.
feedback.proposedChange: Skip placeholder-scan for tests[] and evidence[] paths that exist on disk, or match tokens only inside quoted values rather than file names.

feedback.observation: The refund-request entity was modelled on payment_refund_requests, which nothing writes any more; the live queue (refund_requests, added by a later migration) had no screen and refunds that exhausted automatic retries were invisible.
feedback.proposedChange: Architect pass: for each entity's sourceOfTruth, confirm a current migration or function still INSERTs into it; when a newer table supersedes it, model the newer one.

feedback.observation: With Tailwind 4, an unlayered global rule (.primora-dashboard-skin > aside { position: relative }) overrode the layered 'fixed' and 'z-50' utilities, so the admin phone drawer stayed in the page flow and pushed every screen 1,300 px down. Desktop review could not see it.
feedback.proposedChange: UX review at phone width: check the computed position of every fixed overlay and the top offset of main content; flag unlayered global selectors that target layout elements.

feedback.observation: A PDPL 'anonymize' action wrote Math.random-based phone numbers into a UNIQUE column, colliding between erasures and able to take a real person's number, and discarded the operator's reason.
feedback.proposedChange: Add Math.random (and Date.now-derived identifiers) inside write payloads to the placeholder scan for operator screens; require PII clearing to be one audited server command that writes NULL, not invented values.

feedback.observation: emit --format authz-matrix is derived from the manifest alone, so a privileged function that was never modelled (several admin_* commands were absent until late) or a role-by-table direct write never appears in it; 40 of 70 rows showed no policy. The strongest evidence in this review was a test that enumerates admin-gated functions from pg_proc and calls each as every non-admin role.
feedback.proposedChange: In security-governance.md and verification.md, add a catalog-driven check for stacks with a queryable catalog: list privileged functions and admin-writable tables from the database and diff them against the manifest, and run each as every role expecting an authorization error before any validation error.

feedback.observation: An audit trigger was attached to the eleven tables the console's screens write, while 13 other tables kept FOR ALL admin RLS policies with no trigger, including the ledger, wallet credits and fee rules. 'Every console write is audited' was true of the screens and false of the credential.
feedback.proposedChange: In stack-adapters.md (Supabase), derive the audit-trigger table list from pg_policies (admin policies that allow writes), not from the screens, and require admin-writable money tables to be append-only or command-only.

feedback.observation: The audit decision 'rls-is-sound' and the guidance that RLS is the authorization boundary held for rows but not for columns: public row policies with default column grants exposed admin_notes, Wathq data and staff phone numbers to anonymous callers.
feedback.proposedChange: In stack-adapters.md (Supabase), state that row policies do not restrict columns; every table with a public or broad read policy needs a column-grant or view review for internal fields.

feedback.observation: A deny-list of seven column names was used to keep secrets out of a row-level audit trigger; a PDPL clear command then wrote the cleared name and push token into the append-only log, and the test only checked the phone column.
feedback.proposedChange: In security-governance.md (Audit records), require allow-listed audit columns per table and a test that runs the command's own sensitive fixture through the audit and asserts none of its values appear.

feedback.observation: The security role is told to hold the claim while writing crossCutting, but claim accepts only capability ids, so there is nothing to claim for that section; the only protection is the per-write lock. reviewStatus can also be set on in-progress capabilities although the release rule checks implemented ones, which left it unclear whether a reviewer should wait.
feedback.proposedChange: Let claim take a section name such as crossCutting, and state in multi-agent.md whether reviewStatus may be set before status is implemented.

feedback.observation: Five of the migrations that define the most important policies (harden_auth_and_booking_core, review_fix_booking_core, review_fix_money, review_fix_trust_growth, phone_identity_and_consents) are rejected as evidence by the placeholder content scan because they contain ordinary words such as sample or random, so security evidence had to cite newer files or test files instead of the policy source.
feedback.proposedChange: Scan only manifest-authored text and file names, not the content of cited source files, or let a cited path#Lnn range scope the scan to those lines.

feedback.observation: A reviewer is told to claim the capabilities it reviews, but claim writes capabilities[].owner (the field the reviewer-identity rule compares with reviewedBy) and takes an exclusive lock, so the UX and security reviewers that the multi-agent guide says run in parallel over one domain cannot both hold the same capability.
feedback.proposedChange: Give reviewers a non-exclusive review marker (agents[].reviewing[]) instead of the implementer claim, and keep owner for the implementer only.

feedback.observation: The ux-reviewer contract asks for accessibilityStatus 'with an evidence path', but the screen schema holds only an enum and a single rationale owned by the implementer, so reviewer evidence has nowhere to live except a worklog.
feedback.proposedChange: Add screens[].reviewEvidence[] (paths) and screens[].reviewedBy so a UX pass can attach its checks without overwriting the implementer's rationale.

feedback.observation: A scripted focus sweep (element.focus() on every control) reported nearly every control as having no focus indicator because :focus-visible does not match programmatic focus until a real key press has happened; the first run was a false alarm and only a run after a genuine Tab press was valid.
feedback.proposedChange: In verification.md, tell reviewers to send one real Tab key before any scripted focus sweep and to count controls where :focus-visible did not match, and ship the sweep snippet with the skill.

feedback.observation: Two Tailwind 4 traps hid real defects: 'outline-none focus-visible:outline-2' resolves to outline-style none (no focus indicator on eight inputs), and an unlayered skin rule that sets overflow:hidden on every '[class*=rounded][class*=border]' element silently overrides layered overflow-y-auto, clipping a dialog panel. Both only show at the right viewport height or with real keyboard focus.
feedback.proposedChange: Add both to the UX review checklist: grep for outline-none next to focus-visible:outline-*, and compute overflow/position of every dialog panel against global unlayered selectors at 600 px height.

feedback.observation: The reviewed files were edited by the implementer while the review ran (seven screens changed mid-pass), and the repository fixtures (2 providers, 2 bookings) cannot reproduce pagination, ties, long names or overdue queues, so the review had to build its own data generator and keep re-resolving evidence lines.
feedback.proposedChange: Have the architect record a build ref for each review pass and require the implementer to ship a volume-fixture script; the reviewer cites file#line against that ref.

feedback.observation: The security hardening test 'cover every table an administrator policy can write' finds the tables with the same ILIKE '%is_admin()%' pattern that the migration uses to attach the audit trigger, so it passes by construction and cannot see tables whose administrator check is written inline (invoices, payment_disputes, provider_fee_invoices, psp_reconciliation_runs). The manifest marked the critical gap fixed on the strength of it.
feedback.proposedChange: In verification.md (what the validator and the test suite cannot check) say that a coverage test must derive its target set from behaviour (attempt the write as the role and see whether an audit row appears), never from the predicate the implementation used, and that a reviewer re-derives the set independently before accepting a gap as fixed.

feedback.observation: web_platform/tests/negative-authorization.test.mjs asserts that strings appear in migration and function source and is cited as authorization evidence; the validator's assertion check passes it. It passed for get_booking_address_secure, a function that raises on every call.
feedback.proposedChange: Have validate or the verification reference distinguish tests that execute the boundary (database, HTTP) from tests that read source text, and require at least one executing test per high or critical capability at regulated profile.

feedback.observation: 'set --path qualityGates[x].status --value passed' is refused with evidence-not-resolvable even when the evidence file exists, because the set command is not given a project root and relative evidence paths therefore resolve to nothing. The only way to record a passed gate was --allow-invalid, after which a validate run with --project-root proved the evidence resolves.
feedback.proposedChange: Let add and set accept --project-root (or default it to the parent of .admin-console) so write-time validation resolves evidence the same way validate does.

feedback.observation: The evidence scan removes spaces, hyphens and underscores and then looks for reserved substrings, so real run logs and ordinary prose can match across word boundaries, and any test or file name containing a reserved word (a guard test named for mock data) makes the whole log unusable as evidence. Evidence files had to be rebuilt with those lines left out, and an early version failed because its own explanatory note used a reserved word.
feedback.proposedChange: Scan evidence logs by whole words only (the substring pass is meant for identifiers in implementation fields), or let an evidence file declare the lines it quotes from a command so the scan skips them.

feedback.observation: The qa role file says to claim the domain being audited, but claim records the claimer as the capability owner and holds an exclusive lock, which collides with the reviewer-identity rule and blocks parallel security and UX passes. This QA pass did not claim any capability, for the same reason the UX pass gave.
feedback.proposedChange: Change the qa, security and ux-reviewer role files to register in agents[] and name the audited domain in the agent notes instead of claiming, and reserve claim for implementers.

feedback.observation: Because the PGlite harness reads migrations relative to its own file, copying supabase/migrations and supabase/tests to a scratch folder lets a reviewer weaken one guard per run (edit a migration or append one) without touching the repository; ten of ten weakenings were caught by the new suite and the run takes under two minutes.
feedback.proposedChange: Document the scratch-copy mutation loop in verification.md as the way to 'break the guard locally' for database policies, with the list of weakenings worth trying (drop the identity check, widen a SELECT policy, grant EXECUTE to anon, raise a page cap, replace is_admin with a claim check).

feedback.observation: emit --format gap-report written to stdout raised UnicodeEncodeError (cp1252) once the manifest held Arabic text, so the report was lost with exit 1; the same command with --out works.
feedback.proposedChange: Write emit output as UTF-8 (reconfigure sys.stdout) or document that --out is required on Windows.

feedback.observation: The guard that keeps native dialogs out of the admin screens matches window.prompt( and window.confirm( only, so three bare prompt( calls in the provider screen passed it and the worklog's 'no native prompt is left' was wrong.
feedback.proposedChange: Add to verification.md: a source guard that bans a construct must match every spelling of it (bare, window-qualified, aliased) and should be mutation-checked by adding one violating line.

feedback.observation: The implementer changed several existing tests, including ones the QA pass wrote (the anonymous function allow-list, reason arguments, the expected answer for an owner's direct booking write), because behaviour changed on purpose. The edits were legitimate, but a reviewer can only tell by re-reading the tests against the new behaviour; nothing in the manifest records which test lines changed after review.
feedback.proposedChange: When an implementer edits a test owned by another role, record the file and the reason in the worklog and the reviewer re-runs the file's mutation checks; consider a changelog entry per test file in the manifest.

feedback.observation: An implementer could not set a capability to implemented until serverOperations, authorizationPolicies, tests and evidence were already filled, so status has to be the last field written; and the evidence-token-match rule at regulated profile only passes when a listed test file contains the capability id, a server operation string or a UI route, which was found by failing. Naming each describe block after the capability id satisfied it. Neither build-order.md nor multi-agent.md says so. capability-unreviewed then correctly waits for a different agent.
feedback.proposedChange: In build-order.md (per-capability exit criteria) say: fill implementation fields first and set status implemented last; at regulated profile name the describe block after the capability id so evidence-token-match can resolve.

feedback.observation: The placeholder scan refused evidence files and cited sources because of ordinary vocabulary: HTML placeholder attributes, the SQL function gen_random_uuid, a prose use of the word random, and test or comment text such as mock or sample. Implementers had to cite tests, migrations and components that avoid those words, keep them out of new test titles and comments, and re-resolve every path#Lnn after each edit; a re-runnable idempotent update script per round was the only workable method. Seen on this project and on an earlier one (store: evidence-placeholder-scan, placeholder-scan-jsx-false-positive, test-fixture-scan-boundary).
feedback.proposedChange: Script: scan manifest-authored fields and file names by whole words, not the content of cited source or run-log files; or scope the scan to the cited #Lnn lines. Until then, say in verification.md that evidence files must avoid the reserved words and that evidence line references are re-resolved by script after every edit.

feedback.observation: Dropping a write policy (provider owners updating bookings directly) changes a loud error into an UPDATE that succeeds and changes zero rows, so any client still doing the direct write appears to work. The fix needed a search of every client (web, mobile, edge functions) for direct writers, and the tests had to change from expecting an error to asserting zero rows changed plus unchanged state.
feedback.proposedChange: In security-governance.md or stack-adapters.md (row-level-security stacks): when removing a write path, grep every client for direct writers first, and assert both the refusal or zero-row outcome and that the row is unchanged.

feedback.observation: A SECURITY INVOKER function that reads a table whose read policy was tightened silently changed behaviour: a staff day off stopped removing slots from availability. Making the function SECURITY DEFINER restored availability but changed what it can see (it now reads other customers' bookings), so both the old and the new visibility needed tests.
feedback.proposedChange: In stack-adapters.md (Supabase/Postgres): when tightening a read policy, list every function and view that reads the table and test each from every role before and after; when switching a function to definer, test what it can now see as well as what it now returns.

feedback.observation: Fixing 'audit coverage by behaviour' by attaching a row-level audit trigger to every table, with a name-pattern deny-list for sensitive columns, copied customer names, notes and leave reasons into the permanent audit log and wrote one audit row per affected row on bulk writes. QA found this by attacking the implementer's own fix. The safe shape is default-deny: an allow-list of value-safe tables and columns, and a bulk cap or one summary row per command. A deny-list becomes unsafe the moment coverage widens.
feedback.proposedChange: In security-governance.md (Audit records): audit row values come from a per-table allow-list; widening coverage widens the allow-list deliberately, never the deny-list; bulk writes record one summary row; tests run each command's sensitive fixture through the audit and assert none of its values appear.

feedback.observation: Building one shared dialog primitive surfaced mechanics the reference does not state. Portal the dialog to body before marking siblings inert, otherwise the dialog is inert too. Trap focus and restore it to the opener, falling back to the main region when the opener no longer exists. Streamed framework metadata re-applies the root document title after an effect runs, so a localized title needs re-asserting while the shell is mounted. Reading query parameters on the client needs a Suspense boundary or prerender fails, and history.replaceState keeps filters in the address bar without re-rendering. A Content-Security-Policy is a separate decision.
feedback.proposedChange: In experience-design.md (accessibility and keyboard contracts): add the dialog mechanics as one short paragraph after the APG Dialog binding. Framework specifics (title re-assertion, Suspense) are stack quirks and belong in the project contract unless a second stack confirms.

feedback.observation: experience-design.md requires confirmations to name the command and target, capture a reason and keep input on refusal, but nothing says that browser-native prompt and confirm dialogs cannot do any of that, cannot follow page direction and discard typed input. Every destructive screen had to be rebuilt on a shared command dialog (target facts, consequence, reason, typed confirmation or acknowledgement) plus a yes/no hook. The banned-call guard also missed bare calls (see qa-guard-tests-for-banned-calls-must-match-bare-calls).
feedback.proposedChange: In experience-design.md under the confirmation table: at moderate risk and above, native prompt, confirm and alert do not satisfy the contract; ship one shared command dialog first and guard against every spelling of the native calls.

feedback.observation: Reviewer subagents repeatedly stopped mid-run on account usage limits. Resuming them with an instruction to write partial results to the worklog and manifest first preserved the work; where that had not been done the review would have been lost, since the role files only ask for the worklog at the end of the pass.
feedback.proposedChange: In the ux-reviewer, qa and security role files: write findings to gaps[] and the worklog as each is confirmed, not in one batch at the end, so a pass that is cut off leaves a usable record.

feedback.observation: Changing a 200-line plpgsql function inside a migration by copying its body invites drift. Reading it with pg_get_functiondef, applying a single-line replace, executing the result, and raising an error when nothing changed produced small, reviewable diffs that fail loudly if the base function moved.
feedback.proposedChange: Possible addition to stack-adapters.md (Supabase) migration notes, once a second project confirms.

feedback.observation: The skill ships a harvester agent and the project contract tells every pass to register itself, but agents[].role accepts only architect, implementer, ux-reviewer, qa and security, and agents[].status accepts only active, done and handed-off. The harvester pass could not be registered under its own role or with an in-progress status, and registering it under another role would misstate who did the work.
feedback.proposedChange: Script and schema: add harvester to the agents[].role enum (it must never own capabilities and never count as an implementer or reviewer for the reviewer-identity rule). Docs: until then, state in the harvester role file that it records its pass in its own worklog and not in agents[].

feedback.observation: set on an object-valued field such as a capability's entityStates stores the value as a string, which the lifecycle checks ignore; fixing a wrong object needs a way to replace objects or delete and re-add an item.
add and set cannot remove a screen, capability or entity, so retiring a non-screen (redirect entry) means rewriting a whole array with set.
The placeholder scan reads the whole cited file, so a React file with an input placeholder attribute cannot be cited as evidence for a fixed gap; cite a test instead.

The architect prompt forbids setting capabilities past planned and review states, but a reconciliation of a stale manifest needs statuses corrected; used in-progress for built-and-unreviewed and left review states alone.
About 195 commits of new admin screens and fixes landed without manifest updates; a hook or CI check that fails when a new admin route or admin_ command has no manifest entry would have caught it.

Enforcing aal2 inside is_admin() would have failed ~1,000 existing DB tests; giving the test harness's signed-in users default aal2 claims with a fresh TOTP amr entry (and explicit aal1/stale sessions in negative tests) kept every test meaningful. Worth a note in the skill's Supabase adapter: model the JWT claims the server really checks in the DB test harness.
admin_console_manifest.py set --value '"in-progress"' is refused as an invalid enum and string fields set with json.dumps keep the quotes; plain text must be passed for strings.
feedback.proposedChange: Document in SKILL.md that set --value parses JSON for objects/arrays but stores a quoted JSON string literally (status '"in-progress"' is refused).

feedback.observation: Putting the maker-checker gate inside the existing money command (record a pending request unless an approved request is executing under a one-time token) kept every existing guard (balance, idempotency, audit) on the approver's execution and needed no duplicate money logic.
Enabling TOTP and the MFA hook locally needs supabase stop/start (auth env is fixed at container start); data survives in the docker volume, but the live stack is down for about a minute.
The dispatch said a dev server on :3100 serves this checkout; nothing was listening, so the implementer started one (npm run dev -- -p 3100).

Dropping an admin permissive SELECT policy was not enough: shared helpers (can_access_provider_operation) and public-catalogue policies still let a console session read. A RESTRICTIVE select policy per table (NOT is_admin() OR own row) closed every route at once; dropping admin ALL policies also left orphan write privileges and restrictive write guards that the data-API grant tests flag. Also: I briefly reset two contested reviewStatus values to unreviewed with a bulk set and had to restore them.
feedback.proposedChange: In security-governance.md, recommend a restrictive no-direct-read policy per sensitive table plus revoking write privileges that no permissive policy backs; in the implementer prompt, warn that bulk reviewStatus sets must skip contested capabilities.

feedback.observation: Revoking client privileges was not enough for D-Q8: definer functions run as the table owner, so a blocking trigger had to distinguish sanctioned settling paths (transaction-local GUC set by those functions) and still forbid value growth. pg_trigger_depth() > 1 let PDPL erasure cascades remove customer-side promotional rows while direct DELETEs stay refused.
feedback.proposedChange: In security-governance.md, describe the append-only trigger with a server-path marker plus a 'shares never grow' invariant, and the cascade allowance for erasure.

feedback.observation: admin_console_manifest.py set coerces a JSON-quoted string into a literal with quotes and then rejects it as an invalid enum; strings must be passed raw, lists/objects as JSON.
feedback.proposedChange: Document in the implementer prompt that --value takes raw strings and JSON only for arrays/objects.

feedback.observation: Editing files with Python text mode on Windows silently converted LF to CRLF; patch_function normalises CRLF, but migrations must stay LF (gitattributes) and multi-line search patterns fail on CRLF files.
feedback.proposedChange: Recommend newline='' and explicit CRLF handling in edit helpers on Windows checkouts.
